title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 3 Lesson 1: String Tensions Two Supports custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A particle of weight $W = 60\text{ N}$ is suspended in equilibrium by two light inextensible strings of equal length attached to points at the same horizontal level. Each string is inclined at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal ceiling. By symmetry and resolution, determine the tension $T$ in each string.

A small package of mass $2\text{ kg}$ is suspended in equilibrium by two light strings attached to a ceiling, each making an angle of $45^\circ$ with the vertical. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the tension $T$ in each string correct to 3 significant figures.

A particle of weight $W = 30\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ is supported in equilibrium by two light strings. String 1 is attached to a vertical wall and remains horizontal with tension $T_1$. String 2 is attached to the ceiling and makes an angle of $60^\circ$ above the horizontal with tension $T_2$. Calculate the exact values of $T_1$ and $T_2$.

Two points $A$ and $B$ on a horizontal ceiling are $1.3\text{ m}$ apart. A particle $P$ of weight $26\text{ N}$ is suspended in equilibrium by two light strings of lengths $AP = 0.5\text{ m}$ and $BP = 1.2\text{ m}$. Using the fact that $\triangle APB$ is a right-angled triangle, calculate the tension $T_A$ in string $AP$.

Two light strings attached to a horizontal ceiling support a lamp of mass $M\text{ kg}$ in equilibrium. Each string is inclined at an angle of $20^\circ$ to the ceiling. If each string can withstand a maximum tension of $150\text{ N}$ without breaking, calculate the maximum allowable mass $M$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

A light inextensible string passes over two smooth pegs $A$ and $B$ fixed at the same horizontal level. A mass of $4\text{ kg}$ is attached to each free end of the string and hangs vertically. A block of mass $M$ is attached to the midpoint of the string between $A$ and $B$. In equilibrium, each segment of string between the pegs and the block is inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the mass $M$.

questions.prompt: A particle $O$ of weight $W = 75\text{ N}$ is suspended in equilibrium by two light inextensible strings $OA$ and $OB$ attached to a horizontal ceiling. String $OA$ makes an angle of $40^\circ$ with the ceiling and carries tension $T_A$. String $OB$ makes an angle of $50^\circ$ with the ceiling and carries tension $T_B$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State why $\angle AOB = 90^\circ$, and by resolving forces horizontally, express $T_B$ in terms of $T_A$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces vertically or along the strings, calculate the tension $T_A$ and the tension $T_B$, giving each value correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $m = 1.8\text{ kg}$ is held in equilibrium between two vertical walls by two light inextensible strings. String 1 is attached to the left wall and remains horizontal with tension $T_1$. String 2 is attached to the right wall and makes an angle of $35^\circ$ above the horizontal with tension $T_2$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces vertically in equilibrium, calculate the tension $T_2$ in the inclined string correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces horizontally in equilibrium, calculate the tension $T_1$ in the horizontal string correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A particle of weight $W = 100\text{ N}$ is suspended in equilibrium from two fixed points $A$ and $B$ on a horizontal ceiling. String $A$ makes an angle of $35^\circ$ with the vertical and carries tension $T_A$. String $B$ makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with the vertical and carries tension $T_B$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving horizontally and vertically in equilibrium, write down two simultaneous equations for the tensions $T_A$ and $T_B$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve the equations to determine the tension $T_A$ and the tension $T_B$, giving each value correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $m = 6\text{ kg}$ is suspended from two fixed supports $A$ and $B$ at the same horizontal level by two light inextensible strings of lengths $AP = 1.5\text{ m}$ and $BP = 2.0\text{ m}$. The distance between $A$ and $B$ is $2.5\text{ m}$. A horizontal force of magnitude $F = 15\text{ N}$ is applied to the particle in the direction from $A$ towards $B$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that $\triangle APB$ is a right-angled triangle, and determine the values of $\cos\alpha$, $\sin\alpha$, $\cos\beta$, and $\sin\beta$ for the inclinations of strings $AP$ and $BP$ with the horizontal ceiling.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces horizontally and vertically, calculate the tension $T_A$ in string $AP$ and the tension $T_B$ in string $BP$.

questions.prompt: A small smooth ring $R$ of mass $m = 0.5\text{ kg}$ is threaded onto a light inextensible string of total length $2.8\text{ m}$ whose ends are attached to two fixed points $A$ and $B$ on a horizontal ceiling $2.0\text{ m}$ apart. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain why the string segments $AR$ and $BR$ must make equal angles $\theta$ with the horizontal ceiling, and calculate the exact value of $\cos\theta$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving vertically in equilibrium, calculate the exact tension $T$ in the string in surd form, and evaluate it correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the vertical distance $h$ that the ring hangs below the ceiling, and determine the new tension $T'$ in the string if an additional vertical load of $20\text{ N}$ is suspended from the ring.

questions.prompt: Two fixed supports $A$ and $B$ are located on vertical walls. A particle $P$ of weight $W = 40\text{ N}$ is suspended in equilibrium by two light inextensible strings $AP$ and $BP$. In the initial state, string $AP$ is horizontal and carries tension $T_A$, while string $BP$ makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the vertical and carries tension $T_B$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For this initial equilibrium state, calculate the exact tension $T_B$ in string $BP$ in surd form, and determine the tension $T_A$ in string $AP$ correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A horizontal pushing force of magnitude $F = 20\text{ N}$ is now applied to particle $P$ directed to the left. In the new equilibrium position, string $AP$ is inclined at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal and string $BP$ makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with the vertical. Calculate the new tension $T'_A$ in string $AP$ and the new tension $T'_B$ in string $BP$, giving each value correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $m = 8\text{ kg}$ is suspended in equilibrium by two light inextensible strings $OA$ and $OB$ attached to points $A$ and $B$ at the same horizontal level on a ceiling. String $OA$ makes an angle of $\theta$ with the horizontal ceiling and carries tension $T_A$. String $OB$ makes an angle of $2\theta$ with the horizontal ceiling and carries tension $T_B$, where $0^\circ < \theta < 45^\circ$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
By resolving forces horizontally in equilibrium, show that the ratio of the tensions is given by:
$$\frac{T_A}{T_B} = \frac{\cos 2\theta}{\cos\theta}$$
and explain why $T_B > T_A$ for all $0^\circ < \theta < 45^\circ$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For the case where $\theta = 30^\circ$, calculate the exact values of $T_A$ and $T_B$ in surd form.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Both strings are manufactured from the same material and each will break if its tension exceeds $120\text{ N}$. With $\theta = 30^\circ$, determine which string will break first as the suspended mass is gradually increased, and calculate the maximum mass $M_{\max}$ that can be safely supported.
